title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
data_curation: OpenMLE-Gym provides 5,758 quality-gated executable MLE tasks: 156 Curated Anchors, 3,362 Kaggle Dataset tasks (from MLE-Smith, package-level QC), and 2,240 Kaggle Competition tasks. The competition tasks are filtered from the roughly 11,000-entry Meta Kaggle catalog through leaderboard-length, MLE-Bench-overlap, licensing and rule screens to 3,972, then automated package construction with metric validation to 2,839, then a strict LLM semantic gate to 2,240. The gate scores task validity, data sufficiency, raw-data usage, complexity and data quality, and only 'recommended' tasks are kept. Each package holds raw assets, public data, hidden private answers, prepare.py and metric.py. SFT data (26,259 examples, exact-deduped, at most 32,768 tokens) combines 17,245 Draft solutions (GLM-4.7 and Qwen3-30B teachers, top-4 distinct-score candidates per task) and 9,014 trajectory steps from GLM-4.7-driven AIRA-Evo searches. The trajectory steps end at medal-level endpoints and are filtered by a DeepSeek-V4-Pro causal-inheritance annotator.
curriculum: Pipeline: base model -> execution-grounded full-parameter SFT warm start -> online RL from sandbox execution feedback -> deployment inside the OpenMLE-Evo search harness. SFT collection is budget-adaptive: each task stops sampling at an accepted-example quota or when its execution budget runs out, which shifts verification compute toward sparse-success tasks. SFT runs 3 epochs at LR 3e-5 with cosine decay and 0.1 warmup, global batch 128 and 32K context (SLIME + Megatron-LM). RL samples operators with fixed probabilities (Draft 0.50, Improve 0.17, Debug 0.17, Crossover 0.16) and selects parent states by F(p) = norm(reward) + norm(child-reward variance) + norm(visit-cooling), so training follows informative states rather than a fixed curriculum.
method: Frontis-MA1-35B (from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) and Frontis-MA1-30B (from Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507) are trained as 'meta-evolution agents' on four atomic program-evolution operators (Draft, Improve, Debug, Crossover), the same interface the search harness later composes. RL uses GSPO with TTT-Discover-style reward post-processing: rewards are clip((s - W)/(B - W))^alpha, with adaptive bounds where B is the best observed score and W the 16th-best minus 0.25 times the gap (clamped to static bounds). Entropic leave-one-out advantages exp(beta*c_i)/mean_{j!=i} exp(beta*c_j) - 1 are used, with beta found by bisection so KL(q||Unif) is about log 2. Other settings: clip eps 3.5e-4, TIS on, 16 prompts x 16 samples, 24,576-token responses, Adam LR 1e-6. Rollouts are fully asynchronous (97.0 vs 50.8 min/step, 1.91x). An o3-mini judge flags reward hacking (e.g. shuffled sample submissions) before execution and assigns reward -0.5. At inference, OpenMLE-Evo adds structured experience cards and a board, softmax parent selection over score, gain and novelty (weights 1.0/0.6/0.3), and lazy operator-conditioned memory.
eval_metrics: The primary benchmark is MLE-Bench Lite (22 tasks), with 3 runs per configuration under a 12-hour per-task budget on one RTX 4090 capped at 12 GB VRAM. Metrics are Valid Rate (x/22), Medal Average and Human Rank. Frontis-MA1-35B with OpenMLE-Evo: 21.67/22 valid, 60.61% medals (+/-7.73), Human Rank 0.7647; with OpenMLE-Evo-Max: 22/22, 71.21%, 0.8126. Frontis-MA1-30B: 53.03% (Evo), 66.67% (Evo-Max). References: GPT-5.6 Sol+Codex 72.73%, Kimi K3+Claude Code 72.73%, GPT-5.5+Codex 68.18%, Claude Opus 4.8+Claude Code 63.64%. Transfer is measured on NatureBench Lite (10 tasks, 4h budget) with Match-SOTA (g >= 0) and Surpass-SOTA (g > 0.1). Search efficiency vs original AIRA-Evo: 41.7% fewer total tokens, and new-best updates per 1M tokens rise from 1.77 to 3.27.
key_results: Under the identical OpenMLE-Evo harness, post-training lifts Medal Average from 39.39% (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) to 60.61%, and from 34.85% to 53.03% on the 30B replication. Frontis-MA1-35B with OpenMLE-Evo-Max reaches 71.21%, above GPT-5.5+Codex (68.18%) and approaching GPT-5.6 Sol and Kimi K3 (72.73%). On NatureBench Lite, the trained model raises Match-SOTA from 50% to 70% with the framework fixed, and OpenMLE-Evo raises it from 20% to 50% with the model fixed.
evolution_note: Frontis-MA1 combines three previously separate MLE-agent strands: AIDE/AIRA-style evolutionary search, executable environments (MLE-Dojo, MLE-Smith, MLE-Bench), and RL post-training of MLE agents (ML-Agent, MLE-RL, AceGRPO). Its central move is to train the same Draft/Improve/Debug/Crossover operators that the inference-time evolution composes. It borrows upper-tail entropic advantages from TTT-Discover and asynchronous search from AIRA2. The authors release the full stack (tasks, sandbox, training code, weights) as an open testbed for 'meta-evolution' toward AI4AI recursive self-improvement, and explicitly say it does not yet achieve general autonomous RSI.
